questions.question: May you drop off a passenger for 10 seconds on crossing zig-zag lines?
options: No, stopping and parking are banned on the zig-zags
Yes, if you stay in the car
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 forbids parking or waiting on crossing zig-zag lines.

questions.question: If you want to go straight across a box junction, what must be clear first?
options: The exit road on the far side of the box
Nothing if the light is green
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 says your exit must be clear before entering a box junction.

questions.question: Why might a cyclist wobble or swerve slightly to the right?
options: To avoid potholes, drains, or gusts of wind
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 warns that cyclists need space to avoid drains and road hazards.

questions.question: At 30 mph on a dry road, how big should your gap to the car ahead be?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 requires at least a two-second gap in dry weather.

questions.question: When should you avoid giving a signal?
options: When it could confuse or mislead other road users
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 warns not to give misleading signals.

questions.question: Where do street lights usually show a 30 mph limit for cars unless signs say otherwise?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 explains street-lit roads default to 30 mph unless signed.

questions.question: What light appears immediately after red and amber?
questions.explain: Rule 175: the UK traffic-light cycle is red, then red and amber, then green.

questions.question: What shape is a red-and-white Give Way sign?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 uses the inverted red-and-white triangle for Give Way.

questions.question: A person with a white cane is waiting at a side road you plan to turn into. What should you do?
options: Stop in good time and give way
questions.explain: Rule H2: give extra care and patience to pedestrians who may need more time to cross.

questions.question: Why should you not swing out to the right before turning left?
options: Rule 182 warns it misleads following drivers and risks a crash
questions.explain: Rule 182 says not to swing out to the right before a left turn.

questions.question: What should you do right after checking your mirrors before changing lanes?
options: Check your blind spot over your shoulder
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 says to check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do after you finish overtaking on a two-way road?
options: Move back to the left as soon as it is safe
questions.explain: Rule 160: return to the left side smoothly once you are safely past.

questions.question: What road marking sits across each entrance to a roundabout?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 marks roundabout entrances with broken give-way lines.

questions.question: What signal should you give on approach when taking an exit to the right?
options: No signal until after you leave
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells you to signal right on approach for exits past straight ahead.

questions.question: What signal must you give just before leaving any roundabout?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 requires a left signal as you prepare to leave a roundabout.

questions.question: In which direction do all roundabouts flow in Great Britain?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 186 require clockwise travel on UK roundabouts.

questions.question: When the lights turn green and cyclists are inside the ASL box, what should you do?
options: Give them time and space to move off safely
Edge into the box behind them
questions.explain: Rule 178: let cyclists pull away safely and leave plenty of room when passing.

questions.question: Where must you stop when a traffic light is red?
options: In the middle of the crossroads
questions.explain: Rule 175: you must keep all of your vehicle behind the white stop line.

questions.question: On a two-lane roundabout, where should you position your car?
options: Centred cleanly inside your marked lane
Hugging the grass island on every exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells drivers to keep cleanly within their lane markings.

questions.question: Where should you stop at a STOP sign?
options: In the middle of the junction
Behind the solid white stop line
questions.explain: Rule 171: stop behind the solid white line so your car does not stick out into the main road.

questions.question: Does a flashing amber light at a pelican crossing mean the same as a steady amber light?
options: No, flashing amber means give way to pedestrians on the crossing
questions.explain: Rule 196: at a pelican crossing, flashing amber means let any pedestrians finish crossing, then go if clear.

questions.question: If you approach a roundabout in the wrong lane and traffic is beside you, what is safest?
options: Follow your lane safely and turn around later
Cut across the car beside you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 avoids sudden lane changes across circulating traffic.

questions.question: When can the right-hand approach lane also be used for going straight ahead?
options: When road signs or lane arrows direct straight-ahead traffic into that lane
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 notes that signs and markings can override the default left lane.

questions.question: Does the zig-zag no-overtaking rule apply at signal-controlled crossings like pelican crossings too?
options: Yes, it applies at all pedestrian crossings with zig-zags
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 applies to zebra, pelican, puffin, and toucan crossings with zig-zags.

questions.question: What should you do if a car in front stops inside a box junction and leaves no room on the far side?
options: Wait behind the box line until space opens past the box
Drive onto the yellow lines behind them
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 requires waiting outside the box until your exit is clear.

questions.question: In wet or windy weather, how should you adjust your overtaking gap past a cyclist?
options: Leave even more space than usual
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 advises extra clearance in poor weather or strong side winds.

questions.question: What happens to your view ahead when you leave a proper two-second gap?
options: You can see past the vehicle ahead and spot hazards earlier
You see less of the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 notes a wider gap improves your view of road hazards.

questions.question: If you want to turn into a side road just past a parked car, when do you signal left?
options: After passing the parked car so nobody thinks you are stopping
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 warns that early signals near parked cars can mislead others.

questions.question: What does a round white sign with a black diagonal stripe mean?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 links the national speed limit sign to 60 or 70 mph limits.

questions.question: Does a pedestrian pelican crossing show red and amber to drivers?
options: No, it goes from red to flashing amber, then green
questions.explain: Rule 196: pelican crossings use flashing amber instead of red and amber.

questions.question: What does keeping left help prevent on narrow residential streets?
questions.explain: Rule 160: staying on your side leaves a clear path for oncoming drivers and cyclists.

questions.question: What should you do if a car is already on the roundabout to your right and close?
options: Stop behind the give-way line and wait for a safe gap
Accelerate hard in front of it
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 requires waiting until there is a safe gap.

questions.question: If you signal right on approach, which exit are you telling others you want?
options: An exit to the right (past straight ahead)
The first exit on the left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses a right approach signal for exits past straight ahead.

questions.question: Why should you NOT signal left before passing the exit before yours?
options: Drivers waiting at that earlier exit may think you are turning off and pull out
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 prevents early exit signals from misleading waiting drivers.

questions.question: If you want to make a U-turn at a roundabout, how must you do it?
options: Turn right immediately before the island
Drive all the way around the island clockwise and exit back
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 shows you must travel clockwise around the roundabout to return.

questions.question: Before moving off on green at an ASL, where should you check for cyclists?
options: Your nearside mirror and blind spot, and ahead
questions.explain: Rule 178: check both ahead and to your left in case a cyclist is moving alongside you.

questions.question: What if you accidentally stop with your front bumper over the white line on red?
options: Stop and wait there without entering the crossing or junction
questions.explain: Rule 175: never cross the junction on red; wait safely for green.

questions.question: If parked cars block your view at a Give Way line, what should you do?
options: Edge forward slowly until you can see clearly
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 advises creeping forward safely when parked vehicles block sightlines.

questions.question: On a three-lane road, why should you avoid changing two lanes in one sweep?
options: You cannot check all blind spots and traffic at once
It is only allowed for lorries
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 says to make each lane change carefully with fresh checks.

questions.question: What should you do if you realise you are in the wrong lane on a busy roundabout?
options: Follow your lane safely, take that exit, and turn around later
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 recommends staying safe in your lane rather than cutting across traffic.

questions.question: What happens when variable gantry signs show a speed inside a red ring on a motorway?
options: That lower limit is legally enforced
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 and 258 make red-ring gantry limits legally binding.

questions.question: You see a motorcycle filtering between lanes as you plan to move right. What should you do?
options: Steer right anyway because you are bigger
Hold your lane and wait until the rider has passed safely
Open your door to warn them
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 requires watching for motorcyclists before changing lanes.

questions.question: A lorry on the roundabout is taking the next exit, blocking your view of the lane behind it. What should you do?
options: Wait until the lorry clears so you can see any hidden vehicles behind it
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 warns not to enter when a large vehicle hides traffic to your right.

questions.question: What if a cyclist ahead is in the left lane and intends to turn right at the roundabout?
options: Give them room and do not overtake closely on the approach
Squeeze past them on the left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 warns that cyclists may stay in the left lane even when turning right.

questions.question: Why must you watch the outer lane carefully when joining a two-lane roundabout?
options: A driver in the inner lane might switch outward or a cyclist might be riding there
The outer lane is always closed
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 advises watching all circulating lanes and cyclists before entering.

questions.question: Why do some large roundabouts paint route numbers like 'M6' inside the approach lanes?
options: To help you pick the right lane early for your destination
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses lane markings to guide drivers cleanly through big junctions.

questions.question: May you cross a solid white centre line to pass a cyclist?
options: Only if the cyclist is travelling at 10 mph or less and the way ahead is clear
Yes, at any speed on blind bends
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 129 and Rule 163 allow crossing a solid line to pass a cyclist at 10 mph or less when clear.

questions.question: When you are stopped in a queue, where should you wait if space ends at a zebra crossing?
options: Before the stripes so the crossing stays clear
On top of the black and white stripes
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 and 192 keep crossings clear for people on foot.

questions.question: At a box junction, you follow a tall van and cannot see if space is clear beyond the box. What should you do?
options: Hold back before the box until you can see your exit is clear
Follow the van closely into the box
Overtake the van inside the box
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 means never entering blindly when a tall vehicle hides the exit.

questions.question: If a driver behind is tailgating you, how should you respond?
options: Ease off slightly to leave more space in front so you can brake gently
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 advises increasing your front gap so neither car has to brake sharply.
